title: (chore) O3-6061: Enable one-click releases
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) — Not applicable; CI configuration changes only.
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. — Validated through actionlint, configuration assertions, and GitHub's expression library as described below; PR CI remains to be verified.

## Summary

Enable one-click releases through the **Run workflow** action in OpenMRS CI.

- Add `release_type`, `custom_version`, and `publish_only` inputs with the descriptions, types, and defaults specified in O3-6061.
- Pass these inputs to the shared release workflow, mapping `custom_version` to `release_version` and preserving the `${{ inputs.publish_only || false }}` fallback for push and pull-request events.
- Remove the old `release: created` trigger to prevent duplicate publishing.
- Remove the release job condition that blocked manual runs.
- Add `.github/release.yml` to exclude `openmrs-bot` from generated release notes.

## Screenshots

Not applicable; no UI changes.

## Related Issue

[O3-6061: Add one-click release inputs to CI in openmrs-esm-user-onboarding](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6061)

## Other

The ticket asks to preserve existing job conditions. However, `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly skips manual runs. Keeping it would run the build but skip the release job when a release manager clicks **Run workflow**. Removing this condition is necessary to enable the intended one-click release flow.

Validation completed:

- `actionlint` passes for all local workflows.
- Configuration assertions verify the exact input descriptions, types, defaults, input mappings, trigger removal, manual release eligibility, and bot exclusion.
- Comparison with the original workflow confirms the push/PR triggers, build dependency, secrets, concurrency settings, and all unrelated configuration are unchanged.
- GitHub's `@actions/expressions` library verifies boolean `false` for absent or unchecked publish-only inputs and boolean `true` when selected manually.
- Ten event-routing checks pass against the shared release workflow: upstream PR, normal main push, release/rollback pushes, manual patch/minor/major releases, custom version, publish-only, and a personal-fork manual run.
- `git diff --check` passes.

No real release was triggered. A maintainer should perform the first release after merge.

title: (fix) Declare react-dom as a peer dependency
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This adds `react-dom` to `peerDependencies`, so user onboarding uses the copy the app shell provides instead of loading its own.

The onboarding root component mounts on every page and imports `react-joyride`, which renders through `react-dom`. Without the peer dependency, every page load downloaded a private copy of `react-dom` and `scheduler`.

I built onboarding from `main` and from this branch, swapped each into a build of today's O3 `next`, and ran the same workflows as the 3.8.0 benchmark. Onboarding's JS across the workflows went from 292 KiB to 163 KiB, and the page loads one fewer copy of `react-dom`. The Tutorials modal and a walkthrough rendered with no page errors on both builds.

This is the same change as openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart#3710 and openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management#2784.

title: (chore) Fix the e2e Dockerfile
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Since openmrs/openmrs-distro-referenceapplication#1062, the nightly frontend image ships precompressed `importmap.json` and `routes.registry.json`, and its nginx config serves the `.br`/`.gz` variants before the plain files. The e2e image kept the stale compressed importmap from the nightly image, which points at versioned app directories that the glob `COPY` flattens, so e2e runs time out waiting for the shell to load. This broke e2e CI in several O3 repos starting 2026-08-21.

This copies the frontend files with their directory structure intact and removes the stale compressed variants, so the freshly assembled importmap and routes registry are the ones served. Same fix as openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management#2687.

body:

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Migrates the user-onboarding app's test runner from jest to vitest, aligning it with the patterns already adopted by `openmrs-esm-core`, `openmrs-esm-billing-app`, and the in-flight migrations in `openmrs-esm-template-app` and `openmrs-esm-task-list`.

Changes:
- Replace `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, `@types/jest`, and `identity-obj-proxy` with `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`, and `cross-env`.
- Add `vitest.config.ts`. Keeps the original `jsdom` environment, aliases `@openmrs/esm-framework` to its mock and `react-i18next` to the local `__mocks__` file, inlines `@openmrs/*` deps so Vite processes them, and caps `fakeTimers.toFake` to exclude `queueMicrotask` (otherwise breaks React's scheduler).
- Move the setup file from `src/setup-tests.ts` to `tools/setup-tests.ts` to match the convention used across the other migrated repos. Loads `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` and registers `afterEach(cleanup)`.
- Convert the three test files (`root`, `tooltip`, `modal`) to the vitest API: explicit imports for `describe`/`it`/`expect`/`vi` (plus `beforeEach`/`afterEach` where used), `jest.*` swapped for `vi.*`. In `root.test.tsx`, `jest.mock(name, () => { const actual = jest.requireActual(name); ... })` is rewritten as the async `vi.mock(name, async (importOriginal) => { const actual = await importOriginal<...>(); ... })` form.
- Delete `jest.config.js`.
